elements.quote: Since the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak was reported in December 2019, a huge number of clinical studies have been initiated, firstly in China, South Korea, then subsequently in Europe, Japan, North America and Australia. The number of trials recorded in clinical trial registries is proliferating exponentially, with many independent research efforts designed to answer similar questions.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge (proliferating trials, independent efforts) and uncertainties (small sample sizes, underrepresentation).

elements.quote: As the research landscape becomes increasingly saturated, better coordination in study design, dosing strategies and pooling data for subsequent metanalyses, are needed to ensure definitive answers can be translated into clinical practice as rapidly as possible. Tools that allow researchers to review the diversity of interventions already underway are critical in facilitating collaboration, harmonisation, partnerships and open access research.
elements.reason: The Introduction explains the importance and need for the review (coordination, tools to review diversity) in the context of the saturated research landscape.

The Introduction section does not mention similar systematic reviews or explain the need for the current review in the context of existing reviews, despite feedback suggesting such discussion may be added.
The review focuses on clinical study registrations rather than intervention effects, so describing the mechanism of action of the intervention is not applicable to the rationale.
No logic model is described in the Introduction or retrieved evidence for this review of registrations.

elements.quote: This is a living systematic review of clinical study registrations (clinical trials and otherwise) for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of COVID-19, an important endeavour in the midst of the pandemic and a concurrent infodemic with rapid evidence proliferation.
elements.reason: The Summary section explicitly states the scope and nature of the review, serving as an explicit statement of the objective.

elements.quote: This is a living systematic review of clinical study registrations (clinical trials and otherwise) for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of COVID-19...
elements.reason: The review focuses on clinical study registrations (protocols) rather than synthesizing intervention effects, so the PICO comparison requirement for intervention effects is not applicable.

elements.quote: All clinical trial registrations either being planned, or currently underway to diagnose, treat or prevent COVID-19 were eligible for inclusion in the baseline results of this review. This included patients known to be infected with COVID-19 as well as healthy volunteers, healthcare workers or other patient populations where health related outcomes were assessed in the context of COVID-19. The review was not limited by outcome, language or intervention given the desire to capture all clinical trial registrations planning to or currently evaluating any COVID-19 diagnostic, prevention or treatment modality. Eligibility was not restricted to clinical trials only; no limitations on study design were applied so that all research and observational studies would be incorporated, including retrospective studies.
elements.reason: Specifies population, intervention, study design, and trial status, but does not specify settings or follow-up requirements.

elements.quote: The review was not limited by outcome, language or intervention given the desire to capture all clinical trial registrations planning to or currently evaluating any COVID-19 diagnostic, prevention or treatment modality.
elements.reason: Specifies language (not limited), but does not specify dissemination year or publication/report status.

elements.quote: All clinical trial registrations either being planned, or currently underway to diagnose, treat or prevent COVID-19 were eligible for inclusion...
elements.reason: The review focuses on clinical trial registrations (planned/underway) rather than completed studies with outcome data, making the distinction between outcome measurement and reporting exclusion not applicable.

elements.quote: Definitions of the study designs manually assigned to records in this review were as per the Cochrane Consumers & Communication Review Group Study Design Guide 16 . elements.reason: Groups used in synthesis (study designs) are specified and linked to the analysis.

elements.quote: The results highlight an unprecedented amount of research planned in a remarkably short period of time. While the mobilisation of the scientific community is admirable, this review illustrates a lack of coordination and duplication of effort that will ultimately delay definitive results of key interventions. The expected scientific value of many studies is difficult to gauge, however, limitations of many trial designs are apparent, for instance lack of controlled comparators, and observational studies and trials with inadequate sample size. The proliferation of such studies will likely result in underpowered studies individually unable to generate meaningful evidence for policy makers.
